Subject: RE: DPA redlines (round 1) — privacy counsel notes

Team — reviewed MedTechCo's redline and compiled privacy counsel comments. High level summary below (details in attached response redline):

1) Transfers and SCCs
- We accept SCCs + Redwood EU-US addendum. Counsel requests insertion of a compatibility clause and a statement that customer-initiated transfers follow customer instructions. We'll draft a short addendum and flag the minimal changes.

2) Subprocessor notice & objection
- 30-day notice is more than our current operational window (14 days). Proposed compromise: 14-day notice with a 15-day objection period for "high-risk processing" defined by a short checklist (access to PII, cross-border storage, or security profile). If they object, parties escalate to legal to discuss mitigation or transition plan.

3) Export controls
- Counsel wants a narrowly scoped clause that references compliance with applicable export laws and permits us to suspend processing where required. Avoid broad-sweeping prohibitions that block Dedicated deployments.

4) Evidence & attestations
- We can provide SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and a per-customer server region inventory. For Dedicated/private, we will provide a hardware location attestation letter signed by ops.

5) Execution flow
- Recommend Redwood originate DocuSign envelope with the DPA + EU addendum + signature page. Legal to include execution instructions and contact points. We should allow countersigning via DocuSign or AdobeSign (they indicated DocuSign but be flexible).

Action items:
- Neha: prepare proposed wording for the subprocessor objection carveout and the export-controls clause.
- Priyom: update our redline PDF and include the SCCs + draft EU addendum.
- Jonas: assemble SOC2 redacted report and location attestation template.

Target: send our consolidated response to MedTechCo by Fri 2026-06-05.

Marissa/Lukas — thanks for the quick review. A couple clarifications from counsel side:

- The 30-day notice is intended to give our privacy team time to assess high-risk processors; if Redwood is proposing 14 + 15-day objection (total 29), that's functionally fine as long as the definition of "high-risk" is clear and objective.
- Regarding export-controls: our redline is focused on ensuring we don't inadvertently host PII in jurisdictions with sanctions/export restrictions. We are open to a suspension-based approach as long as we retain the right to terminate if remediation is not possible in a reasonable timeframe.
- Signer: our VP of Legal (Tom Brennan) will execute on the customer side; Alicia will coordinate internal approvals.

Subject: RE: DPA redlines (round 1) — proposed language & execution plan

Team — attached are proposed clause drafts (pasted below) and an execution checklist. Highlights: 

- Subprocessor objection: "Redwood will provide at least fourteen (14) days' written notice of engagement of a new Subprocessor. For Subprocessors that perform High-Risk Processing (defined as processing of Sensitive Personal Data, cross-border storage outside customer's region, or privileged access to systems), Customer shall have fifteen (15) days from receipt of notice to object in writing. If Customer objects, the parties shall meet in good faith to agree mitigation; if unresolved within thirty (30) days, either party may terminate the affected Services or Customer may require Redwood to cease use of that Subprocessor for Customer's Data."

- Export controls: "Each party shall comply with applicable export control laws. If compliance obligations require suspension or cessation of processing in a particular geography, Redwood will notify Customer and take reasonable steps to minimize service disruption. If remediation is not feasible within a commercially reasonable period, Customer may terminate the Agreement with respect to affected Data."

Execution checklist (DocuSign flow):
1) Redwood prepares DPA + SCCs + EU Addendum + signature page
2) Redwood legal / Marissa reviews redline and final PDF
3) Lukas (sales) routes envelope to MedTechCo; MedTechCo signs (Tom Brennan) -> Lukas countersigns (or exec if required)
4) Post-signature: Redwood uploads executed DPA to customer drive and notifies customer success & sales ops

I will update the response PDF and include clause language. Targeting to send to MedTechCo Tues 2026-06-09 AM.
